## Key Insights

1. Rabi Sowing Status: As on December 12, 2025, the area sown under Rabi crops is 536.76 lakh ha (including 84.67 lakh ha in Rapeseed & Mustard & 84.91 lakh ha in Gram) as compared to 512.76 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.
2.  As  on  12.12.2025,  97.49%  of  area  has  been  harvested  for  Kharif  crops  all  over  India. Approximately,  64%  area  of  Pulses  mainly  in  Uradbean  (100%),  Moongbean  (100%)  & Mothbean (100%); 94.46% area of Oilseeds majorly in Groundnut (98.64%),  Soyabean (100%)& Sesamum (96.66%); 95.05% area of Shri Anna cum Coarse Cereals, majorly in Jowar (96.11%) & Bajra (98.31%) and 88% area of Rice has been harvested for crops of Kharif 2025-26.

## 2. Weather Update :

- a) Temperature: Minimum temperatures are likely to be below normal 2-4°C over most parts of the country except northeast & northwest India and Western Himalayan Region, where these are likely to be above normal by 1-3°C during the week.
- b) Rainfall  Distribution: From  October  01-  December  14  2025,  the  All-India  cumulative rainfall  is  17%  higher  than  its  Long  Period  Average (LPA), with regional variations:  (i) East & Northeast India: 3%; (ii) Northwest India: 46%; (iii) Central India: 38%; and South Peninsula: 7%.
3.  A fresh feeble Western Disturbance is likely to affect western Himalayan region from the night of 17 th  December 2025.
4.  Light  rainfall/snowfall  at  isolated  places  over  Jammu-Kashmir-Ladakh-Gilgit-BaltistanMuzaffarabad on 15 th  and  over  Himachal Pradesh and over Arunachal Pradesh during 15 th  -17 th  December.
5.  Thunderstorm  and  lightning  with  gusty  winds  very  likely  at  isolated  places  over Andaman & Nicobar Islands during 15 th  - 18 th  December.
6.  Cold wave conditions very likely to prevail at isolated places over Telangana and Interior Karnataka on 15 th  and 16 th  with severe cold wave conditions likely to prevail over North Interior Karnataka on 15 th  December.
7.  Dense fog conditions very likely to prevail during early hours/morning hours in isolated pockets of Northeast India during 15th-19th, Himachal Pradesh during 15th-17th, Punjab, Haryana,  Chandigarh,  Uttar  Pradesh,  northeast  Madhya  Pradesh  on  15th  &  16th December.

## 3. Inputs Situation

- a) Water  Reservoir  Status :  As  on  11  December  2025,  the  total  live  water  storage  in  166 important  reservoirs  across  the  country  (monitored  by  CWC)  is  155.226  billion  cubic meter,  which  is  84.5%  of  total  live  storage  capacity  (183.565  BCM).  The  current  year's storage is  nearly 107.44 percent of last  year's storage  and 122.23 percent of the average storage of the last ten years during the corresponding period. The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.
- b) Groundwater  Levels :  In  August  2025,  around  89%  of  the  country's  monitoring  stations exhibited a depth to water level within 10 meters below ground level. Deeper water levels of more than 20 m are observed in around 5% of stations of the country covering mainly the western states, especially Western Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh.
3.  The deeper groundwater level in the states like Western Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh during August 2025 has been significantly influenced by the over extraction of groundwater compared to the recharge during the monsoon period.
4.  Annual water level comparison with the previous year August 2024 to August 2025 has shown  that  about  56.5%  of  total  analyzed  stations  of  the  country  experienced  rise  in annual water level fluctuation because of the higher rainfall in 2025 compared to 2024 in Monsoon period.
5.  About 70% of the analyzed stations of the unconfined aquifer experienced a rise of water level  in  the  decadal  mean  water  level  fluctuation  of  2015-2024  with  respect  to  August 2025.
- c) Seeds  and  Fertilizers :  For  Kharif  2025,  certified  seed  availability  is  178.64  lakh  quintals against  a  requirement  of  164.05  lakh  quintals, ensuring  a  surplus of  14.60  lakh  quintals. The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products.
4. Pests  &  Diseases :  There  is  no  major  pest  incidence  that  has  been  reported.  The  overall intensity of pests and diseases remained below the Economic Threshold Level.

## 1. RAINFALL

-  During the week (04 Dec - 10 Dec 2025), lower rainfall was observed, as compared to Long Period Average (LPA) by 55%. Cumulative seasonal rainfall (01 st Oct to 10 Dec 2025) is higher than LPA by 20%.

<!-- image -->

## Rainfall Forecast:

-  Overall, rainfall activity is likely to be below over the country except Western Himalayan Region and northwest plains, where it is likely to be near normal to above normal.

## 2. TEMPERATURE: MIN & MAX

## Temerature

## Week 1 (12 Dec - 18 Dec 2025):

-  No  significant  change  in  minimum  temperature  very  likely  over  plains  of  Northwest, Maharashtra  India  during  next  2  days,  rise  by  2-4°C  during  subsequent  4  days  and  no significant change thereafter.

## Details of each Segment

-  No significant change in minimum temperature very likely over Central India for next 24 hours, rise by 2-4°C for subsequent 4 days and no significant change thereafter.
-  No significant change in minimum temperature over remaining parts of the country during next 7 days

## Week 2 (19 Dec - 25 Dec 2025):

-  Minimum temperatures are likely to be below normal 2-4°C over most parts of the country except northeast & northwest India and Western Himalayan Region, where these are likely to be above normal by 1-3°C during the week.
-  Cold  wave  conditions  are  likely  to  prevail  in  isolated  pockets  over  interior  Odisha, adjoining Chhattisgarh, East Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha, and Telangana during some days of the week.
-  Dense fog conditions  likely  to  prevail  during  early  morning  hours  in  isolated  pockets  of Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana Chandigarh & Delhi and Rajasthan during some days of the week.

## 3. Crops

## Rabi Crops - Area coverage

-  Wheat: About 275.66 lakh ha (88% of normal) area coverage under Wheat has been reported as compared to 258.48 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.
-  Rapeseed & Mustard : About 84.67 (107% of normal) lakh ha area coverage under Rapeseed &  Mustard  has  been  reported  as  compared  to  81.16  lakh  ha  during  the  corresponding period of last year.
-  Gram: About 84.91 (84% of normal) lakh ha area coverage under Gram has been reported as compared to 81.67 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.

## 5. REMOTE SENSING BASED SOIL MOISTURE OBSERVATION

## Soil Moisture Observation

-  Soil moisture during 04 Dec - 10 Dec is similar/better than the average of the past 9 years in major parts of M.P, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Haryana, Punjab, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Telangana, A.P. and Bihar.

Key Insights

1. Rabi Sowing Status: As on December 12, 2025, the area sown under Rabi crops is 536.76 lakh ha (including 84.67 lakh ha in Rapeseed & Mustard & 84.91 lakh ha in Gram) as compared to 512.76 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.
2.  As  on  12.12.2025,  97.49%  of  area  has  been  harvested  for  Kharif  crops  all  over  India. Approximately,  64%  area  of  Pulses  mainly  in  Uradbean  (100%),  Moongbean  (100%)  & Mothbean (100%); 94.46% area of Oilseeds majorly in Groundnut (98.64%),  Soyabean (100%)& Sesamum (96.66%); 95.05% area of Shri Anna cum Coarse Cereals, majorly in Jowar (96.11%) & Bajra (98.31%) and 88% area of Rice has been harvested for crops of Kharif 2025-26.

2. Weather Update :

- a) Temperature: Minimum temperatures are likely to be below normal 2-4°C over most parts of the country except northeast & northwest India and Western Himalayan Region, where these are likely to be above normal by 1-3°C during the week.
- b) Rainfall  Distribution: From  October  01-  December  14  2025,  the  All-India  cumulative rainfall  is  17%  higher  than  its  Long  Period  Average (LPA), with regional variations:  (i) East & Northeast India: 3%; (ii) Northwest India: 46%; (iii) Central India: 38%; and South Peninsula: 7%.
3.  A fresh feeble Western Disturbance is likely to affect western Himalayan region from the night of 17 th  December 2025.
4.  Light  rainfall/snowfall  at  isolated  places  over  Jammu-Kashmir-Ladakh-Gilgit-BaltistanMuzaffarabad on 15 th  and  over  Himachal Pradesh and over Arunachal Pradesh during 15 th  -17 th  December.
5.  Thunderstorm  and  lightning  with  gusty  winds  very  likely  at  isolated  places  over Andaman & Nicobar Islands during 15 th  - 18 th  December.
6.  Cold wave conditions very likely to prevail at isolated places over Telangana and Interior Karnataka on 15 th  and 16 th  with severe cold wave conditions likely to prevail over North Interior Karnataka on 15 th  December.
7.  Dense fog conditions very likely to prevail during early hours/morning hours in isolated pockets of Northeast India during 15th-19th, Himachal Pradesh during 15th-17th, Punjab, Haryana,  Chandigarh,  Uttar  Pradesh,  northeast  Madhya  Pradesh  on  15th  &  16th December.

3. Inputs Situation

- a) Water  Reservoir  Status :  As  on  11  December  2025,  the  total  live  water  storage  in  166 important  reservoirs  across  the  country  (monitored  by  CWC)  is  155.226  billion  cubic meter,  which  is  84.5%  of  total  live  storage  capacity  (183.565  BCM).  The  current  year's storage is  nearly 107.44 percent of last  year's storage  and 122.23 percent of the average storage of the last ten years during the corresponding period. The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period.
- b) Groundwater  Levels :  In  August  2025,  around  89%  of  the  country's  monitoring  stations exhibited a depth to water level within 10 meters below ground level. Deeper water levels of more than 20 m are observed in around 5% of stations of the country covering mainly the western states, especially Western Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh.
3.  The deeper groundwater level in the states like Western Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh during August 2025 has been significantly influenced by the over extraction of groundwater compared to the recharge during the monsoon period.
4.  Annual water level comparison with the previous year August 2024 to August 2025 has shown  that  about  56.5%  of  total  analyzed  stations  of  the  country  experienced  rise  in annual water level fluctuation because of the higher rainfall in 2025 compared to 2024 in Monsoon period.
5.  About 70% of the analyzed stations of the unconfined aquifer experienced a rise of water level  in  the  decadal  mean  water  level  fluctuation  of  2015-2024  with  respect  to  August 2025.
- c) Seeds  and  Fertilizers :  For  Kharif  2025,  certified  seed  availability  is  178.64  lakh  quintals against  a  requirement  of  164.05  lakh  quintals, ensuring  a  surplus of  14.60  lakh  quintals. The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products.
4. Pests  &  Diseases :  There  is  no  major  pest  incidence  that  has  been  reported.  The  overall intensity of pests and diseases remained below the Economic Threshold Level.
